items.summary: server.js hard-codes a Stripe secret-key-style string (STRIPE_KEY) in source and uses it in the /charge handler; the value looks like a fixture placeholder but the pattern is a committed secret. gitleaks did not run, so git history (single commit) was only checked by hand and no .env file is tracked. ST-3.
evidence: searched: .env files and key prefixes (sk_, AKIA, ghp_, xox, private key) in git ls-files; only server.js:11 matched
items.fix: Read the key from process.env (STRIPE_SECRET_KEY), keep it out of git, and rotate it if it was ever real. Run gitleaks over history.

items.summary: Key rotation and whether any keys were shared with an AI tool cannot be seen from the repo.
evidence: searched: rotation notes or secrets docs in repo; none
items.question: When were the Stripe and database credentials last rotated, and were any pasted into an AI assistant, chat or screenshot?

items.summary: No package.json or lockfile is committed, so the dependencies (express, cors, ./db) cannot be verified, and packages.json ran offline with zero packages. Also, ./db is required but not in the repo.
items.question: Show the real package.json and lockfile, and the ./db module, so dependency names can be verified against the registry.

items.summary: No manifest, lockfile, Dependabot/Renovate config or CI audit step exists in the repo.
items.fix: Commit package.json and a lockfile, install with npm ci, enable Dependabot and add npm audit to CI.

items.summary: The server is a JSON-only API and renders no HTML. No frontend is in the repo, so XSS cannot be assessed here.
SQL is built by string interpolation of request input in signup, login, forgot and invoices, giving direct SQL injection (login bypass, data theft, account takeover via reset_token update).
items.fix: Use parameterised queries (db.query('... WHERE email = $1', [email])) in every handler and validate id as an integer.

items.summary: Authentication returns a token in the JSON body and no cookies or sessions are used, so classic CSRF does not apply. Revisit if the token moves to a cookie.
No server-side fetch of user-supplied URLs, redirects or file-path building exist. The only outbound call goes to a fixed Stripe URL.
CORS is open to every origin on all routes, including the charge and invoice endpoints.
items.fix: Set cors({ origin: [your app origins] }) from config; avoid '*' once credentials or cookies are used.

items.summary: No security headers are set: no helmet or manual HSTS, CSP, X-Content-Type-Options or frame protection, and Express sends X-Powered-By.
items.fix: Add helmet() before routes and disable x-powered-by; confirm with curl -I on the live site.

items.summary: Database and TLS configuration are not in the repo (./db is absent) and nothing in server.js redirects HTTP or terminates TLS. Stripe calls use https.
items.question: Show the DB connection settings (sslmode), the TLS terminator or host config, and the provider's at-rest encryption setting.

items.summary: IAM, DB credential privileges and who holds production access cannot be seen from the repo. Note the Stripe key is a full secret key rather than a restricted key.
items.question: Which DB user does the app connect as (superuser?), and who and what (including AI agents) hold production credentials?

items.summary: The code has no logging at all, so no sensitive data is logged, but it also records no audit of who did what. Passwords are also handled with an unsalted MD5 hash (see identity domain) and the full Stripe response, including charge details, is returned to the client.
items.fix: Add a structured logger with redaction of Authorization, password and card fields, and log authentication and charge events with actor and request ID. Return only the fields the client needs from /charge.

items.summary: No error handler exists and all handlers are async without try/catch, so a DB error (easily triggered by injection) leaves requests hanging or crashes the process on unhandled rejection in modern Node; the default Express handler prints stack traces unless NODE_ENV=production. The /charge handler also relays Stripe's raw error body to the client.
items.fix: Add async error wrapping (or express-async-errors), a final error middleware returning a generic message, and set NODE_ENV=production.
